__readme: Shared parity fixtures for the versioned eval SUITE FILE contract. Loaded by sdk/tests/eval-suite-file.test.ts in mcpjam-inspector (Zod: evalSuiteFileSchema in sdk/src/contract/suite-file.ts) and intended to be loaded VERBATIM by the hand-mirrored Convex validators in mcpjam-backend. The backend cannot import @mcpjam/sdk into convex/ default-runtime code, so this file is the only common ground truth — copy it byte for byte, do not re-author it. LOAD RULE: strip EVERY key whose name starts with '__' before handing a row to a validator; they are fixture annotations (__label, __why, __kind, __structural) and every object in this contract is closed, so a row that still carries them would be rejected for the wrong reason — turning an accept row into a false failure and, worse, a reject row into a false success. DISPATCH: '__kind' selects the validator; every row here is 'suiteFile'. '__structural' on a reject row records whether the GENERATED JSON Schema (sdk/src/contract/eval-suite.schema.json) must also reject it: true means the rejection is expressible in JSON Schema, false means it is a cross-field rule only the Zod validator (and a hand-mirrored equivalent) enforces. A false-flagged row is asserted to be ACCEPTED by the JSON Schema, so the flag can never rot into decoration. 'roundTrip' rows are validated, canonicalized, re-parsed and re-validated; they must deep-equal the original, which is what proves no default was materialized. When the contract shape changes, edit the Zod schema, regenerate the JSON Schema, AND edit this fixture in the same PR.

reject.__label: assertion declaring BOTH discriminators (kind and type)
reject.__why: The two assertion vocabularies are disjoint by construction: `kind` is a DOM-level WidgetAssertion, `type` is a transcript Predicate. An object carrying both is ambiguous, and resolving it is worse than refusing it — the widget branch is closed and rejects the stray `type`, while the predicate branch is open and would accept the same object, strip every widget field, and silently turn "the word 'Refunded' is on screen" into "no tool errors occurred". The second passes almost always, so the eval goes green while checking something nobody asked for.
